1.32 Replace a damaged original with its intact conversion

Symptom. An original DNG is truncated on disk: Lightroom cannot build a preview or reports the file as damaged, and editing fails, yet Finder, Quick Look or sips thumbnails look fine. Elsewhere, an earlier converter’s output of the same exposure, such as an Adobe DNG Converter run kept on /Volumes/Backup, is intact.

Prerequisites. Detect damage at the pixel level, not from preview renders. Thumbnailing tools such as sips render the embedded preview, which can be complete while the raw data behind it is truncated. A full raw decode, a pixel comparison in DNG Compare, or a header showing a declared raw strip or tile running past the file’s stable length establishes the damage; see Classify identity. Then prove the conversion is the same exposure (capture time, camera and serial, exposure UID) and that its own raw data decodes in full. Record the damaged file’s path, exact name, SHA-256 and size, and the photo’s develop settings and history as Lightroom shows them.

Mechanism. Lightroom finds an original by its path and name. Putting an intact file of the same exposure at that exact path and name lets the existing catalog record, with its edits, history, virtual copies, collections and cloud association, point at readable raw data again, without re-registration.

Quit Classic normally. Move the damaged files aside to a folder outside every catalog folder, mirroring their relative paths, and keep them. Copy the conversion to the original’s path under the original’s exact name and extension, and check the copy’s SHA-256 against the conversion. Reopen Classic, select that folder, and rebuild its previews through Library → Previews (standard or 1:1, and Smart Previews where the photos had them).

Do not write the catalog, re-import the file, or use Read Metadata from Files to clear a metadata badge: the conversion’s embedded XMP is not the catalog’s current state. Resolve any badge with Reconcile catalog, XMP, ratings and dates.

Verify. In Lightroom, the folder shows no missing or damaged-file badges, and each replaced photo renders at Fit and 100% from the new original. Develop settings, history, virtual copies and collection membership match what you recorded. On disk, the placed file’s SHA-256 equals the conversion’s, and the damaged files remain intact in the side folder.

Undo. Quit Classic, move the conversion out, return the damaged file to its path and name, and rebuild the folder’s previews. The catalog was not changed by the swap, so nothing else needs reversing.

Limits. Lightroom’s registered fingerprint and any cloud original were computed from the old bytes and are not updated by the swap; duplicate detection and Sync may treat the new file differently. Develop history was made against the old file’s raw data: a conversion with a different crop, opcodes, linear or mosaic data, or converter version can render the same settings differently, so inspect every replaced photo in Lightroom rather than assuming equality. This is a procedure, not a retained native control in this cookbook’s evidence table.
